minutes.headline: Assessors debated the senior deferral process; a motion to contact lien holders first was withdrawn, and no limits were voted.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors heard the principal assessor's update on Vision Appraisal cyclical inspections starting next Tuesday. It reviewed the senior means-tested exemption brochure, application and suggested income and asset limits, with no vote on the numbers. A long debate on a tax deferral process ended with a motion to contact lien holders first being withdrawn, and the board entered executive session at the end.

votes.motion: Allow the principal assessor to put the cyclical inspection schedule on the website when completed.
Approve the March 12 executive session minutes for release.
Amend the deferral process so the lien holder is contacted first.
votes.outcome: not audible (seconded, then motion and second withdrawn at about 5993; no vote taken)

votes.motion: Adjourn and enter executive session under MGL c.59 s.60 and c.214 s.1B to discuss the deferral application.
votes.outcome: passed (seconded, all in favor, no count)

budget_items.what_was_said: Number of inspections due by June 30 stated; the principal assessor questioned a mailing charge that she says was not explicit in the contract.
The assessor thinks Vision will charge per callback visit when appointments are scheduled.
Suggested limits from Concord discussed for single, head of household and joint filers; other towns' numbers compared.
An asset limit figure was proposed for the application; the board has not voted on it.
A sample from another community showing a maximum exemption amount and income levels.
A member said the last time attention was diverted from the assessor's office it cost the town a large sum.
The assessor notified the finance director that the board approved a figure for the 2026 overlay; a 2024 anomaly was raised.
The assessor urged keeping the MUNIS consultant under contract ahead of the cloud upgrade; a member noted cost is higher.

decisions.decision: The principal assessor will post the cyclical inspection schedule on the town website once finalized.
Next meeting set for April 2 to review the senior exemption process and numbers; another is April 16.
The assessor reorganization concern, with the lead assessor reporting to the finance director, will be put on the next agenda.
Organizational performance metrics will stay on the April 2 agenda.
The Clause 41 and 17 warrant article item will be dropped from the next agenda and revisited before town meeting.
The lien-holder-first motion was withdrawn and the deferral process will be discussed further next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors withdrew a motion to contact the lien holder first in the tax deferral process; no vote was taken and the process returns next meeting.
The board reviewed a senior means-tested exemption brochure, application and suggested income and asset limits, and took no vote on any limit.
The board voted to let the principal assessor post the Vision Appraisal cyclical inspection schedule on the town website once it is completed.
The principal assessor questioned a mailing charge she says the Vision contract did not state explicitly, and expects per-callback visit charges.
The board voted to release the March 12 executive session minutes, then entered executive session at the end of the meeting.

why_it_matters: The senior exemption limits and the deferral process decide which older homeowners can reduce or postpone a tax bill, and neither has been settled yet.
Vision's cyclical inspections begin soon, and possible extra charges under the contract bear on what the revaluation work costs the town.
